retirement_age.notes: Statutory retirement age is 66 for pensions starting from 1 February 2025 and rises to 67 for pensions starting from 1 February 2030. The same age applies to employees, the self-employed and civil servants. Early retirement is possible with long careers (for example age 63 with 42 years).

open_questions: Next federal election: sources indicate it is expected in 2029 (IPU lists an expected date of 2029-06-30 at https://data.ipu.org/parliament/BE/BE-LC01/election/BE-LC01-E20240609/; the Flemish Parliament page says June 2029). No exact date has been officially set in the sources found, so the date is left null.

The retirement age source is a Belgian law-firm summary of the pension law; the official Federal Pensions Service (SFP/FPD) page was not retrieved. Supporting sources (https://english.n-va.be/news/government-reaches-agreement-on-new-pension-law, https://www.loyensloeff.com/insights/news--events/news/belgiums-pension-reform-early-retirement-and-the-bonusmalus-impact-for-hr/) agree on 66 now and 67 from 2030. The stored value 66 will change to 67 for pensions starting on 1 February 2030.

Prime Minister has no fixed term; term_ends is null. The current Chamber of Representatives was elected on 2024-06-09 with five-year terms (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Belgian_federal_election).
The monarch holds the office without a set term; term_ends is null on that basis.

De Wever's birth date and swearing-in date (2025-02-03) come from Simple Wikipedia, consistent with English Wikipedia, Wikiwand and the France 24 report of the swearing-in; no official federal government page was retrieved.
The political_system phrase is based on a descriptive reference page (https://planetrulers.com/belgium-king/); verify against an official source if wording matters.
